lessons.title: Short Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Short Questions

What do you mean by tolerance?

Tolerance means respecting the opinions, beliefs and customs of others. It means living peacefully with people who differ from us in religion or culture. Islam teaches tolerance toward all people, including non-Muslims. A tolerant society avoids hatred and conflict and promotes harmony.

What is meant by co-existence?

Co-existence means different communities living together peacefully in one society. Each group keeps its own identity, faith and customs while respecting others. It requires justice, equality and mutual respect among citizens. Pakistan's ideology supports co-existence for all its religious communities.

Define modernism.

Modernism means adopting new ideas, science and technology for progress. It does not mean abandoning one's religion or culture. In an Islamic state, modernism works within Islamic values. It helps a nation meet the challenges of the modern world.

What is meant by ideology?

Ideology is a set of beliefs and principles that guide the life of a nation. It gives a nation its identity, purpose and direction. Pakistan's ideology is based on Islam, which guides its politics and society. It unites the people and motivates them to work for common goals.

Define foreign policy.

Foreign policy is the set of principles by which a country deals with other countries. It protects national interests, security and independence. Pakistan's foreign policy is based on peace, friendship and Islamic brotherhood. It seeks good relations with all countries, especially Muslim states.

What is Two-Nation Theory?

The Two-Nation Theory states that Muslims and Hindus are two separate nations. They differ in religion, law, culture, heroes and way of life. Therefore Muslims needed a separate homeland where they could live by Islam. This theory became the basis of the Pakistan Movement and the creation of Pakistan.

Write a short note on Iqbal's Allahabad address of 1930.

In his 1930 Allahabad address, Allama Iqbal gave the idea of a separate Muslim state. He proposed uniting the Muslim-majority provinces of north-western India. He argued that Islam is a complete way of life, not merely a religion. His address gave the Pakistan Movement its clear political goal.

What did Quaid-i-Azam say in his Karachi address of 1943?

In 1943 at Karachi, Quaid-i-Azam explained the meaning of Pakistan's demand. He said the Muslims wanted a homeland where Islamic principles would rule. He stressed unity, discipline and faith among the Muslims. He assured minorities that their rights would be fully protected in Pakistan.

lessons.title: Detailed Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Detailed Questions

Discuss how Islam is the ideological basis of Pakistan.

Pakistan was created on the basis of the Islamic ideology. The Muslims of the subcontinent were a separate nation on the basis of religion, culture, law and heroes. Islam gives a complete code of life, covering belief, worship, social life and government. The Two-Nation Theory held that Hindus and Muslims could not live as one nation. The Objectives Resolution of 1949 made Islam the basis of the constitution and declared the sovereignty of Allah.

Discuss the basic principles of the Islamic ideology.

The first principle is the oneness of Allah (Tauheed), which gives unity to life. The second is the finality of Prophethood, which gives guidance through the Quran and Sunnah. The third is justice and equality for all citizens, regardless of religion or race. The fourth is accountability before Allah, which makes rulers answerable to the people. Other principles are tolerance, brotherhood, democracy and respect for human rights.

Explain how Islam promotes peace and tolerance.

Islam teaches peace, tolerance and respect for all human beings. The Last Sermon declared all human beings equal and forbade wronging others. The Quran says there is no compulsion in religion (2:256). Non-Muslim minorities are given protection of life, property and worship. Islam commands good treatment of neighbours, women and even enemies in war.

Discuss the basic principles of an Islamic welfare state.

The sovereignty of Allah is supreme and the rulers are His trustees. Justice and equality before the law apply to rulers and subjects alike. Consultation (Shura) guides the government in public affairs. The state protects life, property and honour of every citizen. The welfare of the poor is secured through Zakat, Bait-ul-Mal and state help for the needy.

Write a note on Pakistan as a modern Islamic state in the light of the ideas of Iqbal and Quaid-i-Azam.

Iqbal wanted a state where Islamic principles guide modern progress. He believed Islam encourages reason, science and democracy. Quaid-i-Azam wanted a democratic state with rule of law and equal citizenship. He said Pakistan would be a modern state, not a theocratic state ruled by priests. Both leaders wanted a state that is Islamic in values and modern in institutions.

lessons.title: Short Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Short Questions

Who is a Muslim according to the Constitution of 1973?

According to the Constitution, a Muslim believes in the oneness of Allah. He believes in the finality of the Prophethood of Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH). He believes in the revealed books and in the Day of Judgement. A person who does not believe in the finality of Prophethood is declared non-Muslim.

Write a short note on the Sovereignty of Allah.

The Sovereignty of Allah means that all authority in the universe belongs to Allah. The people of Pakistan exercise authority as a trust from Allah. No law can be made against the Quran and Sunnah. This principle is stated in the Objectives Resolution and the Constitution of 1973.

What is meant by judicial review?

Judicial review is the power of courts to examine laws and government actions. If a law is against the Constitution, the court can declare it void. This power protects fundamental rights of citizens. It keeps the legislature and executive within constitutional limits.

Why was the Constitution of 1962 repealed?

The Constitution of 1962 was imposed by one man and lacked popular support. It gave too much power to the President and limited political parties. The people demanded a democratic and parliamentary constitution. After the fall of Ayub Khan, the 1962 Constitution was abrogated in 1969.

When and by whom was the Constitution of 1956 repealed?

The Constitution of 1956 was abrogated in October 1958. President Iskandar Mirza abrogated it and imposed martial law. General Ayub Khan then took power as the Chief Martial Law Administrator. The first constitution of Pakistan thus lasted only about two and a half years.

What is the status of the Governor of a province?

The Governor is the constitutional head of the province. He is appointed by the President of Pakistan. He acts on the advice of the Chief Minister and the provincial cabinet. He gives assent to provincial laws and represents the federation in the province.

When and by whom was the government of Junejo dismissed?

The government of Prime Minister Muhammad Khan Junejo was dismissed in May 1988. President Zia-ul-Haq dismissed it using the powers of the Eighth Amendment. He also dissolved the National Assembly at the same time. This dismissal is an example of the use of Article 58(2)(b) in Pakistan's history.

Write the duties of the Council of Islamic Ideology.

The Council of Islamic Ideology advises the government on Islamic matters. It examines laws and suggests whether they agree with the Quran and Sunnah. It recommends ways to bring existing laws into conformity with Islam. It also guides the government on Islamic education and social matters.

lessons.title: Detailed Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Detailed Questions

Discuss the role of political parties in developing democracy in Pakistan.

Political parties organise public opinion and give the people a political programme. They contest elections and form the government or sit in opposition. They train leaders and educate voters about their rights and duties. They link the people with the government and present public demands. A healthy party system develops democratic culture and peaceful transfer of power.

Discuss the reasons and impacts of the separation of East Pakistan.

East and West Pakistan were separated by about a thousand miles of Indian territory. The language issue, economic disparity and political deprivation created a sense of neglect. The results of the 1970 elections were not accepted and the political crisis deepened. Indian interference and the war of December 1971 led to the fall of Dhaka. East Pakistan became Bangladesh, and Pakistan lost more than half of its population.

Discuss the salient features of the Constitution of 1973.

The Constitution of 1973 is written, federal and parliamentary in nature. Islam is the state religion, and no law can be repugnant to the Quran and Sunnah. It guarantees fundamental rights, including freedom, equality and security of person. It provides an independent judiciary and a bicameral parliament. The President is the head of state and the Prime Minister is the chief executive.

Discuss the role of the judiciary in Pakistan.

The judiciary interprets the Constitution and the laws of the country. It protects the fundamental rights of citizens through judicial review. It settles disputes between the federation and the provinces. An independent judiciary keeps the government within the law and ensures justice.

Discuss the salient features of the Constitutions of 1956 and 1962.

The Constitution of 1956 was the first constitution of Pakistan and declared it an Islamic Republic. It provided a parliamentary system, One Unit and Urdu and Bengali as national languages. It remained in force for two and a half years and was abrogated in 1958. The Constitution of 1962 provided a presidential system and the system of Basic Democracies. It contained Islamic provisions but was abrogated in 1969 after public agitation.

Discuss the Islamic provisions of the Constitution of 1973.

Islam is declared the state religion of Pakistan and the sovereignty of Allah is recognised. No law can be made repugnant to the Quran and Sunnah. The Second Amendment defines a Muslim and declares Ahmadis non-Muslims. The Council of Islamic Ideology advises on bringing laws in line with Islam. Steps are promised for Quranic teaching, Zakat, Ushr and the elimination of interest.

Discuss the structure of the Federal Government under the Constitution of 1973.

The President is the head of state and performs his duties on the advice of the Prime Minister. The Prime Minister and the Cabinet run the administration of the federation. Parliament consists of the National Assembly and the Senate and makes federal laws. The Supreme Court heads the judiciary and interprets the constitution. Federal ministries work under secretaries, and the Council of Common Interest settles federal-provincial matters.

mcqs.why: The detailed notes say the first constitution of 1956 declared Pakistan an Islamic Republic and provided a parliamentary system.

mcqs.q: The Constitution of 1962 provided which system of government?
mcqs.why: The notes state that the Constitution of 1962 provided a presidential system along with the system of Basic Democracies.

mcqs.why: The notes list the promised steps as Quranic teaching, Zakat, Ushr and the elimination of interest; Zakat and Ushr are to be promoted, not eliminated.

Short Questions

Write the number of members of the Kashmir Council.

The Kashmir Council has 14 members. Eight members are from Azad Jammu and Kashmir and six are representatives of the Government of Pakistan. The members from Azad Kashmir include its President, Prime Minister and six members of the Legislative Assembly. The Council is chaired by the Prime Minister of Pakistan.

Who is the Chairman of the Gilgit-Baltistan Council?

The Prime Minister of Pakistan is the Chairman of the Gilgit-Baltistan Council. The Council has 12 members, six nominated by the Prime Minister and six elected by the Gilgit-Baltistan Legislative Assembly. It is an administrative institution for Gilgit-Baltistan.

What is the article of the Constitution that deals with the administrative power of the provinces?

Provincial administrative power is dealt with in the Constitution under the federal scheme. The provinces exercise authority over subjects in the provincial field. Their executive authority is exercised by the Governor on the advice of the cabinet. This arrangement is part of the federal distribution of powers in the 1973 Constitution.

At which places are the circuit benches of the High Court of Azad Kashmir located?

The High Court of Azad Kashmir has three circuit benches. They are located at Kotli, Mirpur and Rawlakot. These benches make justice accessible to the people of different districts.

What are the levels of Local Government?

Local government in Pakistan works at the district, tehsil and union council levels. In cities it works through metropolitan corporations, municipal committees and town committees. Each level has elected members and a head, like the Nazim or Mayor. These bodies look after local services such as water, sanitation and roads.

What are the duties of a Chief Officer?

The Chief Officer is the administrative head of a local council. He carries out the decisions of the council and supervises its staff. He prepares the budget and keeps the accounts of the council. He is responsible for the day-to-day administration of local services.

What is the status of the President of Azad Kashmir?

The President of Azad Jammu and Kashmir is the constitutional head of the state. He is elected by the Azad Kashmir Legislative Assembly and the Kashmir Council. He acts on the advice of the Prime Minister of Azad Kashmir. He represents the state and gives assent to laws passed by the Assembly.

Where is the Supreme Appellate Court of Gilgit-Baltistan located?

The Supreme Appellate Court of Gilgit-Baltistan is located at Gilgit. It is the highest court of appeal in Gilgit-Baltistan. It hears appeals against the decisions of the Chief Court. Its Chief Judge is appointed in the manner laid down for the region.

Detailed Questions

Discuss the duties of the Federation under the Constitution of 1973.

The Federation performs its duties in the name of the President. It looks after defence, foreign affairs, currency and communications. It coordinates between the provinces and settles their disputes. The Council of Common Interest distributes resources and announces NFC Awards. The Federation also protects the country against external aggression and internal disorder.

Discuss the structure of the Government of Gilgit-Baltistan.

Gilgit-Baltistan has a Governor and a Chief Minister heading its government. It has a Legislative Assembly elected by the people of the region. It has a Council chaired by the Prime Minister of Pakistan. Its courts are the Chief Court and the Supreme Appellate Court.

Discuss the relations between the Federation and the Provinces.

The Constitution divides powers between the federation and the provinces. The federation controls defence, foreign affairs and currency. The provinces control police, health and agriculture, among other subjects. The Council of Common Interests settles disputes and coordinates policy between them.

Discuss the relationship between the provinces and the local governments.

Under Article 140-A of the Constitution of 1973, provinces must establish local governments. Provincial assemblies pass laws for local governments and devolve administrative and financial powers to them. Provinces give funds to local governments through the Provincial Finance Commission. Local governments work under provincial supervision but manage local affairs themselves. This system brings government closer to the people at the grass-root level.

Discuss the duties of the provinces.

Provinces maintain law and order and run the police and provincial administration. They look after health, education, agriculture and local government. They make laws on provincial subjects through the Provincial Assembly. They collect provincial taxes and prepare the provincial budget. They implement federal laws and cooperate with the federation in national matters.

Discuss the duties of the District Council and the Tehsil Council.

The District Council plans and carries out development work in the whole district. It provides water supply, sanitation, roads and health and education facilities. The Tehsil Council performs similar duties within its tehsil. Both councils are formed with the chairmen of Union Councils as members. The Chief Officer, a senior government servant, acts as secretary and supervises all departments.

Discuss the duties of the Metropolitan Corporation.

The Metropolitan Corporation is headed by the Mayor and looks after a big city. It plans the city, builds and repairs roads, and provides street lights. It arranges water supply, sewerage, cleanliness and public parks. It controls buildings and markets and protects public health. It collects municipal taxes and spends them on city services.

Short Questions

Write a short note on human rights in Islam.

Islam gave human rights fourteen centuries before modern declarations. The Last Sermon declared the life, property and honour of every person sacred. Islam grants equality regardless of colour, race or language. It protects the rights of women, children, minorities and even enemies in war.

Define rights.

Rights are the freedoms and claims that every human being has by birth. They are recognised and protected by law and by society. Rights enable a person to live with dignity and develop fully. They are balanced by duties toward others and toward the state.

Write a short note on economic rights.

Economic rights allow a person to earn a living and own property. They include the right to work, to fair wages and to trade. Islam forbids interest, hoarding and dishonest trade, protecting economic justice. The state must provide opportunities so that no citizen starves.

Who approved the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and when?

The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was approved by the United Nations. It was adopted by the General Assembly on 10 December 1948. It lists civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights. Pakistan, as a UN member, supports these rights in its Constitution.

Write two political rights.

The right to vote in free and fair elections is a political right. The right to form political parties and take part in government is another. Citizens may also stand for election and hold public office. These rights make the government answerable to the people.

Define duties.

Duties are the obligations a citizen owes to the state and to fellow citizens. They include obeying the law, paying taxes and respecting the rights of others. A citizen must be loyal to the state and honest in voting and public dealing. Rights and duties go together: every right of one person is the duty of another. Performing duties well makes a citizen useful to society.

Write a Quranic verse about economic rights or its translation.

The Quran says: 'And give the orphans their property' (Surah Al-Nisa, 4:2). It also says: 'And do not devour one another's wealth unjustly' (Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:188). These verses protect the right to own, earn and use property lawfully. They forbid usurping the wealth of orphans and the weak. Economic rights in Islam thus rest on justice and honest dealing.

Write two social rights.

The right to education is a social right of every citizen. The right to health care and a clean environment is another social right. Social rights also include protection of family and childhood. The state provides schools, hospitals and welfare for these rights.

Detailed Questions

Discuss the concept of human rights.

Human rights are the rights every human being has simply by being human. They include the right to life, liberty, equality, dignity and security. They are not given by any government; governments only recognise and protect them. Islam, constitutions and international law all affirm these rights. When human rights are respected, society becomes peaceful and just.

Discuss the rights given by Islam.

Islam gives the right to life: no one may kill an innocent person. It gives the right to property, honour and freedom of belief. Women have rights to inheritance, education and respect in society. Non-Muslims in an Islamic state have protection of life, property and worship. These rights were declared in the Quran and the Last Sermon of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

Discuss the Universal Declaration of Human Rights of 1948.

The Declaration was adopted by the United Nations on 10 December 1948. It has thirty articles covering civil, political, economic and social rights. It declares all human beings free and equal in dignity and rights. It forbids slavery, torture and arbitrary arrest. Though not a treaty, it guides the constitutions and laws of member states.

Discuss the nature of basic human rights in Pakistan.

The Constitution of 1973 guarantees fundamental rights to every citizen. These include security of person, freedom of speech, association and religion. All citizens are equal before the law and cannot be discriminated against. An arrested person must be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours. These rights are enforceable by the courts and have an Islamic basis.

Compare the rights given under the Constitution of Pakistan with the human rights of the United Nations.

The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was approved by the United Nations in 1948. It contains 30 articles and applies to all human beings in the world. The Constitution of Pakistan of 1973 gives fundamental rights to the citizens of Pakistan. These rights are enforceable through the courts, while the UN Declaration is recommendatory. Both agree on life, liberty, equality, justice and freedom of thought and religion.

Short Questions

Write four objectives of education.

Education develops the personality and character of the individual. It prepares citizens who can serve society and the country. It provides knowledge and skills needed for work and progress. It preserves culture and values and promotes national unity.

Differentiate between vocational and general education.

General education gives broad knowledge in languages, science and social studies. It develops thinking and prepares students for higher studies. Vocational education trains students in a particular trade or skill. It prepares them directly for a job, like plumbing, tailoring or computer work.

What is informal education?

Informal education is learning that takes place outside schools. A child learns manners, language and values from family and society. It has no fixed syllabus, timetable or examination. It continues throughout life through experience and observation.

What is the concept of education?

Education is the process of developing the mind, character and abilities of a person. The word comes from a Latin root meaning to bring up or to lead out. It includes teaching, training and the growth of values. True education makes a person useful to himself and to society.

Classes ninth and tenth are called by which name?

Classes ninth and tenth together are called secondary education. Secondary education lasts for two years in Pakistan. It ends with the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examination. After SSC, students enter higher secondary or intermediate education.

Write a short note on information technology in education.

Information technology has changed teaching and learning in Pakistan. Computers, the internet and multimedia make lessons interesting and clear. Students can study online and access books from anywhere. Teachers use technology for presentations, tests and record keeping.

Write a short note on the education of special persons.

Special persons include children with hearing, sight or physical difficulties. They need special schools, trained teachers and assistive devices. Pakistan has special education centres in many districts. With proper support, special children can learn skills and live independent lives.

What is the distance education system?

In distance education, students study at home instead of attending classes daily. Lessons are sent by post, radio, television or the internet. Allama Iqbal Open University is the largest distance education institution in Pakistan. It allows working people and women to continue their studies.

Detailed Questions

Discuss the educational objectives of Pakistan.

The educational objectives of Pakistan are described in the Constitution of 1973 and education policies. Education should develop students as responsible citizens in the light of Islamic ideology. It should create an effective framework for training teachers and design curricula on Quranic principles. It should use computers for effective learning, increase literacy and focus on women's education. It should prepare students for vocational and technical education and protect the ideology of Pakistan.

Discuss four areas of vocational education in Pakistan in detail.

Medical Education: Doctors and paramedical staff are needed to maintain human health, so the government has set up medical colleges and universities where students are admitted after F.Sc. through an entry test, and nursing institutions train hospital staff. Engineering Education: Engineering is of paramount importance for industrial development; the minimum qualification is F.Sc., the degree takes four years, and polytechnics and engineering colleges teach civil, mechanical, electrical and mining fields. Law Education: Law education is essential for justice and order; an LLB is required to become a judge or lawyer, and five-year LLB, LLM, LLD and Sharia Law programmes are offered in universities. Agricultural Education: Pakistan is basically an agricultural country and most people live in villages; the government has set up agricultural institutions and universities to replace old cultivation methods and raise production. The chapter also covers Business and Commerce, Computer and Information Technology, Home Economics and Teacher Training.

Discuss the stages of education in Pakistan.

Education in Pakistan begins with primary education, classes one to five. Elementary education covers classes six to eight, and secondary covers nine and ten. Higher secondary or intermediate education covers classes eleven and twelve. After that come graduate, postgraduate and professional education in universities.

Discuss the problems of education in Pakistan and give suggestions to solve them.

Problems include a shortage of trained teachers and school buildings. Many children drop out because of poverty and child labour. The syllabus is often outdated and examinations encourage rote learning. Suggestions are: increase the education budget and train teachers better. Provide free books and stipends, update the syllabus and improve examination methods.

Write a note on: Education of special persons in Pakistan, Distance Education in Pakistan, Madrassa Education System in Pakistan.

Education of special persons: Special children need special attention, trained teachers and suitable institutions; the government promotes special education so that such children can become useful members of society. Distance Education: Allama Iqbal Open University teaches through the distance method, using books, radio, television and now online means, so that students who cannot attend regular institutions can still study. Madrassa Education System: Madrassas provide religious education and are now being brought into the mainstream by adding modern subjects, so that their students can also join general and professional fields.

Short Questions

What are the mental benefits of sports?

Sports reduce stress and anxiety and improve mood. They build confidence, discipline and the spirit of teamwork. Games teach players to accept victory and defeat gracefully. They sharpen the mind through quick decisions and strategy.

Name the four prominent wrestlers of Pakistan.

The four prominent wrestlers are Gama Pehlwan, Bholu Pehlwan. Imam Bakhsh Pehlwan and Jhara Pehlwan are the other two. They made Pakistan famous in wrestling in South Asia. Their matches drew huge crowds and inspired young wrestlers.

What is the purpose of PTDC?

The Pakistan Tourism Development Corporation (PTDC) promotes tourism in Pakistan. It develops tourist resorts, hotels and transport for visitors. It publicises the historical and natural beauty of Pakistan abroad. It earns foreign exchange and creates jobs for local people.

Write two problems of tourism in Pakistan.

Poor roads, hotels and transport make travel difficult for tourists. Security concerns and a weak international image reduce the number of visitors. There is also a shortage of trained guides and tourist information. These problems limit the income Pakistan earns from tourism.

Write two suggestions to promote tourism in Pakistan.

The government should build better roads, hotels and rest houses at tourist places. Pakistan's historical sites and northern valleys should be advertised abroad. Tourist police and guides should be trained to help visitors. Visa rules for tourists should be made simple and friendly.

In which countries is Kabaddi popular?

Kabaddi is popular in Pakistan, India and Bangladesh. It is also played in Iran, Nepal and Sri Lanka. It is the national game of Bangladesh and a popular rural sport in Punjab. International Kabaddi tournaments are now held regularly in Asia.

How many Hockey World Cups has Pakistan won, and in which years?

Pakistan has won the Hockey World Cup four times. It won in 1971, 1978, 1982 and 1994. No other country has won the World Cup four times. Pakistan is therefore the most successful team in World Cup history.

How many Olympic hockey championships has Pakistan won, and in which years?

Pakistan has won the Olympic hockey gold medal three times. It won in 1960 at Rome, in 1968 at Mexico City and in 1984 at Los Angeles. These victories made Pakistan a world power in hockey. The 1960 victory broke India's long Olympic winning streak.

How is the Malakhara game played?

Malakhara is a popular Sindhi wrestling game, like Japanese Sumo wrestling. It is an effort to defeat the opponent by making him fall while he is standing. Malakhra wrestlers show their skill at melas throughout Sindh and win appreciation. Thousands of people from distant areas come to watch this cultural game.

Describe the relationship between sports and tourism.

Sports and tourism are both healthy activities that give discipline, courage, passion and mental peace. Sports events attract tourists, such as the Shandur Polo tournament watched by visitors from the whole world. Tourists learn the history and geography of the places they visit and enjoy local games. Both activities build personality, a healthy society and the economy of the country.

Detailed Questions

Discuss the importance of sports in human life.

Sports keep the body healthy and protect against disease. They teach discipline, punctuality and respect for rules. Team games develop cooperation, leadership and sportsmanship. Sports also provide entertainment and bring nations closer through competitions.

Give an overview of Pakistan's performance in Hockey and Cricket.

Hockey: Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup four times, in 1971 at Barcelona, 1978 at Buenos Aires, 1982 in India and 1994 at Sydney. Pakistan won three Olympic gold medals, in 1960 at Rome, 1968 at Mexico and 1984 at Los Angeles, besides three silver and two bronze medals. Cricket: The International Cricket Council allowed Pakistan to play international cricket in 1952, and Pakistan played its first Test against India at Delhi on 16 October 1952. Pakistan won the Cricket World Cup in 1992 against England, scoring 249 runs while England were bowled out for 227, with Wasim Akram as Player of the Match. Pakistan has also won the T20 World Cup once and the Champions Trophy once.

Discuss Pakistan's performance in Squash and Snooker.

Squash: Jahangir Khan and Jansher Khan made Pakistan famous in squash, and Pakistan produced seven British Open champions, though no Pakistani reached a British Open final after 1997. Snooker: Muhammad Yusuf won the IBSF World Snooker Championship at Johannesburg in 1994, beating Johnson of Iceland 11-9. Muhammad Asif won a medal at Dubai in 2012 and the IBSF World Snooker Championship at Sofia, besides the IBSF World Six Red Team Championship at Carlow, Ireland in 2013 with Muhammad Sajjad. Ahsan Ramadan became the youngest world champion at the age of 16 in March 2022.

Discuss the status of any three indigenous (Desi) sports of Pakistan.

Kabaddi: Kabaddi is mostly played in the villages of Punjab and also in India, Canada, America, Iran, England and Sri Lanka; the first Kabaddi World Cup was held in 2010 and won by India, while Pakistan got success in the Kabaddi World Cup of 2020. Malakhra: Malakhra is a popular Sindhi wrestling game like Japanese Sumo, in which the wrestler tries to make his opponent fall while standing, and it is shown at melas throughout Sindh. Wrestling: The golden period of Pakistani wrestling runs from Muhammad Azeem Gama Pehlwan to Imam Bakhash and Manzoor Ahmad Bholu Pehlwan, who dominated world wrestlers; Bholu Pehlwan won the title of Rustam-e-Pakistan in 1949 and was awarded Tamgha-e-Imtiaz in 1962.

Discuss the problems of tourism in Pakistan and give suggestions for their solution.

Problems: There is lack of transportation for tourists, terrorism from which foreign tourists feel insecure, lack of infrastructure, inadequate accommodation at tourist destinations, lack of government patronage and negligence of concerned agencies. Suggestions: The transport system should be improved and law and order made satisfactory by controlling terrorism. Cleanliness at touring places should meet international standards and accommodation should be available at cheap rates. Where possible, chair lifts should be provided in hilly areas, and more funds should be given to the Tourism Development Corporation so that tourist places can be developed.

Write a note on the tourist places of Pakistan.

Pakistan has the northern valleys of Hunza, Swat and Naran with snow-capped peaks. It has historical places like Lahore Fort, Badshahi Mosque and Mohenjo-Daro. The beaches of Karachi and the deserts of Thar attract many visitors. The Kalash valley, Murree and Ziarat are famous for their natural beauty and culture.

lessons.title: Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Activities

Activity for the Teacher: Tell the students about wrestling and show them a video if possible.

The teacher tells the class about the famous wrestlers of Pakistan, such as Gama, Imam Bakhash, Bholu and Jhara Pehlwan. A video of wrestling is shown to the students if possible. Students discuss the golden period of Pakistani wrestling and its present condition. The activity creates interest in the traditional sports of the country.

Activity for the Teacher: Prepare a chart of the World Kabaddi Cups, showing where they were held and who won them.

Students collect information about the Kabaddi World Cups held so far. They prepare a chart showing the year, the venue and the winning country of each Cup. The chart is displayed in the classroom. The activity teaches students to organise sports information in a clear form.

Activity for the Teacher: Ask the students to point out historical and tourist sites on a map.

Students take a map of Pakistan and mark historical and tourist places on it. They point out places such as Lahore Fort, Badshahi Masjid, Mohenjo Daro and the valleys of Swat and Kaghan. Each student tells the class one fact about a place he has marked. The activity improves map reading and knowledge of the country.

Activity for the Students: Get information about Archery and Gullidanda from your parents and exchange it with your classmates.

Students ask their parents about Archery and Gullidanda, two traditional games. They note how each game is played and where it is popular. In the class, students exchange this information with one another. The activity connects classroom learning with family knowledge.
